sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Sanjay Kumar Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner
 Shri K. K. Tiwari-Govt. Adv. appearing on behalf of Ad
 General.
ORDER 1] Heard finally with the consent of the parties.

2] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of Cr.P.C./Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.122/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 506, 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860,
registered at Police Station Lasudiya, District Indore, and all other consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number.
3] Counsel for the petitioner, at the outset, has submitted that the parties have settled their disputes amicably out of the Court.

It is also submitted that no purpose would be served to keep the matter pending when the matter is already compromised; the interlocutory applications and the affidavit regarding which are also filed.
In such circumstances, the petition may be allowed.
4] Counsel for the respondent No.2 has submitted that he has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37574 2 MCRC-17743-2024 5] Counsel for the respondent/State has submitted that appropriate order may be passed.

1 6] On due consideration of submissions, and on perusal of the documents filed on record, this Court has no hesitation to allow the present petition.

sentences.text: 7] Accordingly, the petition is hereby allowed, and the FIR FIR bearing Crime No.122/2024 for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 506, 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered at Police Station Lasudiya, District Indore, and all other consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number, pending against the petitioner, are hereby quashed.
8] All the interlocutory applications are hereby disposed of.
9] Accordingly, the petition stands allowed and disposed of.
